verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              यथा जयार्थिनः सेनां नयन्ति भरतर्षभ। ईषद्धर्मं प्रपीड्यापि तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said By what means does a man become sinful, by what does he acquire virtue, by what does he acquire renunciation, and by what does he acquire Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              सत्येन हि स्थितो धर्म उपपत्त्या तथा परे। साध्वाचारतया केचित्तथैवौपयिकादपि॥२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said now You know all duties. This question which you have put to me is only for confirmation of your conclusions. Listen fully to Liberation, and Renunciation, and Sin, and Virtue.

verses.sanskrit: उपायधर्मान्वक्ष्यामि सिद्धार्थानर्थधर्मयोः। निर्मर्यादा दस्यवस्तु भवन्ति परिपन्थिनः॥३॥
verses.english: Perceiving any one of the five objects, desire runs after it at first. Indeed, obtaining them within the pale of the senses, O foremost of Bharata's family, desire or hatred originates.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां प्रतिविघातार्थं प्रवक्ष्याम्यथ नैगमम्। कार्याणां सर्वसिद्ध्यर्थं तानुपायान्निबोध मे॥४॥
verses.english: One then, for the sake of that object, trics and begins acts that require much labour. One tries his best for enjoying again and again those forms and scents that appear very sweet.

verses.sanskrit: उभे प्रज्ञे वेदितव्ये ऋज्वी वक्रा च भारत। जानन्वक्रां न सेवेत प्रतिबाधेत चागताम्॥५॥
verses.english: Gradually, attachment, hatred, greed and errors of judgement originate, answer

verses.sanskrit: अमित्रा एव राजानं भेदेनोपचरन्त्युत। तां राजा निकृतिं जानन्यथाऽमित्रान्प्रबाधते॥६॥
verses.english: The mind of one possessed by greed and mistake and affected by attachment and hatred is never bent to virtue. One then begins with hypocrisy to do deeds which are good.

verses.sanskrit: गजानां पार्थ वर्माणि गोवृषाजगराणि च। शल्यकण्टकलोहानि तनुत्रचमराणि च॥७॥
verses.english: Indeed, with hypocrisy one then tries to acquire virture and with hypocrisy one likes to acquire riches. When one succeeds, O son of Kuru's family, in acquiring riches with hypocrisy, one gives his heart to such acquisition wholly. It is then that a person begins to do sinful acts, despite the admonitions of well-wishers and the wise, to all whom he makes reasonable conformable to the scriptural injunctions.

verses.sanskrit: सितपीतानि शस्त्राणि सन्नाहाः पीतलोहिताः। नानारञ्जनरक्ताः स्युः पताकाः केतवश्च ह॥८॥
ऋश्यस्तोमराः खड्गा निशिताश्च परश्वधाः। फलकान्यथ चर्माणि प्रतिकल्प्यान्यनेकशः॥९॥
अभिनीतानि शस्त्राणि योधाश्च कृतनिश्चयाः। चैत्र्यां वा मार्गशीर्ष्यां वा सेनायोगः प्रशस्यते॥१०॥
verses.english: Begotten of attachment and mistake, his sins of three sorts, rapidly multiply for he thinks sinfully, speaks sinfully, and acts sinfully.

verses.sanskrit: पक्वसस्या हि पृथिवी भवत्यम्बुमती तदा। नैवातिशीतो नात्युष्णः कालो भवति भारत॥११॥
verses.english: When he clearly begins to commit sin, the good notice his wickedness. Those, however, who are sinfully disposed contract friendship with him.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्तदा योजयेत परेषां व्यसनेऽथवा। एते हि योगाः सेनायाः प्रशस्ताः परबाधने॥१२॥
verses.english: He cannot acquire happiness even here. Whence then would he succeed in acquiring happiness hereafter? It is thus that one becomes sinful. Listen now to me as I describe to you one who is righteous.

verses.sanskrit: जलवांस्तृणवान्मार्गः समो गम्यः प्रशस्यते। चारैः सुविदिताभ्यासः कुशलैर्वनगोचरैः॥१३॥
verses.english: Such a man, seeking, as he does, the wellbeing of others, succeeds in acquiring good for himself. By doing duties which are fraught with other people's well-being, he attains at last to a highly agreeable end.

verses.sanskrit: न ह्यरण्येन शक्येत गन्तुं मृगगणैरिव। तस्मात्सेनासु तानेव योजयन्ति जयार्थिनः॥१४॥
verses.english: He who, helped by his wisdom, succeeds beforehand seeing the faults referred to above, who is skilled in determining what is happiness and what is sorrow and how each is engendered, and who waits respectfully upon the good, makes progress in acquiring virtue, both on account of his habit and such companionship of the good. The mind of such a person finds pleasure in virtue, and he live on, making virtue his stay.

verses.sanskrit: अग्रतः पुरुषानीकं शक्तं चापि कुलोद्भवम्। आवासस्तोयवान्दुर्गः पर्याकाशः प्रशस्यते॥१५॥
verses.english: If he wishes to acquire riches, he wishes only such wealth as inay be gained in righteous ways.

verses.sanskrit: परेषामुपसर्पाणां प्रतिषेधस्तथा भवेत्। आकाशात्तु वनाभ्याशं मन्यन्ते गुणवत्तरम्॥१६॥
verses.english: In fact, he waters the roots of only thosc objects in which he sees merit. Thus does not become righteous and make friends with the good.

verses.sanskrit: बहुभिर्गुणजातैश्च ये युद्धकुशला जनाः। उपन्यासो भवेत्तत्र बलानां नातिदूरतः॥१७॥
उपन्यासावतरणं पदातीनां च गूहनम्। अथ शत्रुप्रतीघातमापदर्थं परायणम्॥१८॥
verses.english: On account of his acquisition of friends, of riches, and of children, he sports happily both here and hereafter. The mastery that a living being acquires over sound, touch, taste, forin, and scent, O Bharata, represents the fruit of virtue. Remember this. Having acquired the fruit of virtue, O Yudhishthira, such a man does not yield to joy.

verses.sanskrit: सप्तर्षीन्पृष्ठतः कृत्वा युध्येयुरचला इव। अनेन विधिना शत्रून् जिगीषेतापि दुर्जयान्॥१९॥
verses.english: Without being satisfied with such fruits of virtue he follows Renunciation, led on by the eye of knowledge, When, having gained the eye of knowledge he ceases to find pleasure in the gratification of desire, in taste and in scent, when he does not allow his mind to run towards sound, touch and form, it is then that he succeeds in freeing himself from desire. He does not, however, even then renounce virtue or righteous acts.

verses.sanskrit: यतो वायुर्यतः सूर्यो यतः शुक्रस्ततो जयः। पूर्वं पूर्वं ज्याय एषां सन्निपाते युधिष्ठिर॥२०॥
verses.english: Seeing then all the worlds as being subject top destruction, he tries to renounce virtue and tries to attain to Liberation by the (well-known) means.

verses.sanskrit: अकर्दमामनुदकाममर्यादामलोष्टकाम्। अश्वभूमिं प्रशंसन्ति ये युद्धकुशला जनाः॥२१॥
verses.english: Gradually renouncing all sinful deeds he follows Renunciation, and becoming righteoussouled succeeds at last in acquiring Liberation.

verses.sanskrit: अपङ्का गर्तरहिता रथभूमिः प्रशस्यते। नीचद्रुमा महाकक्षा सोदका हस्तियोधिनाम्॥२२॥
verses.english: I have now told you, O Son, of that about which you had asked me, viz., the topics of Sin, Righteousness, Renunciation, and Liberation, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: बहुदुर्गा महाकक्षा वेणुवेत्रसमाकुला। पदातीनां क्षमा भूमिः पर्वतोपवनानि च॥२३॥
verses.english: You should, therefore, O Yudhishthira, follow virtue under all circumstances. Eternal is the success, O son of Kunti, of you who follow righteousness.

verses.sanskrit: पदातिबहुला सेना दृढा भवति भारत। रथाश्वबहुला सेना सुदिनेषु प्रशस्यते॥२४॥
verses.english: An army, O Bharata, which has a large infantry, is considered very strong. An army which has a greater number of cars and horsemen is considered to be very powerful in a clear day.

verses.sanskrit: पदातिनागबहुला प्रावृट्काले प्रशस्यते। गुणानेतान्प्रसंख्याय देशकालौ प्रयोजयेत्॥२५॥
verses.english: An army, again, which consists of a greater number of infantry and elephants becomes effective in the rains. Having carefully observed these points, the king should devote his attention to the characteristics of place and time.

verses.sanskrit: एवं संचिन्त्य यो याति तिथिनक्षत्रपूजितः। विजयं लभते नित्यं सेनां सम्यक्प्रयोजयन्। प्रसुप्तांस्तृषितान् श्रान्तान् प्रकीर्णान्नाभिघातयेत्॥२६॥
verses.english: That king, who, having attended to all these points, marches, under a proper constellation and an auspicious luminary, always succeeds in acquiring victory by properly leading his troops.

verses.sanskrit: मोक्षे प्रयाणे चलने पानभोजनकालयोः। अतिक्षिप्तान्व्यतिक्षिप्तान् निहतान्प्रतनूकृतान्॥२७॥
verses.english: No one should kill the sleepy, or the thirsty, or the fatigued, or one whose armours have fallen away, or one who has set his heart on final liberation, or one who is flying away, or one who is walking along a road, or one engaged in drinking or eating, or one who is mad, or one who is insane, or one who has been wounded morally, or one who has been greatly weakened by his wounds, or one who is residing confidentally, or one who has begun any task without having been able to finish it, or one who is a master of some particular art, or one who is in grief, or one who goes out of the camp for procuring forage or fodder, or men who pitch camps or are camp-followers, or those who wait at the gates of the king or of his ministers, or his menials, or the head of such servants.

verses.sanskrit: अविश्रब्धान्कृतारम्भानुपन्यासात्प्रतापितान्। बहिश्चरानुपन्यासान्कृतवेश्मानुसारिणः॥२८॥
पारम्पर्यागते द्वारे ये केचिदनुवर्तिनः। परिचर्यावतो द्वारे ये च केचन वर्गिणः॥२९॥
अनीकं ये विभिन्दन्ति भिन्नं संस्थापयन्ति च। समानाशनपानास्ते कार्या द्विगुणवेतनाः॥३०॥
verses.english: Those of your warriors who break the ranks of enemies, or rally your retreating soldiers, should have their pay doubled and should be honoured by you with food, drink, and seats equal to your own.

verses.sanskrit: दशाधिपतयः कार्याः शताधिपतयस्तथा। ततः सहस्राधिपतिं कुर्याच्छूरमतन्द्रितम्॥३१॥
verses.english: The heads of ten soldiers amongst them should be made heads of a hundred. And the careful hero who is the head of a hundred soldiers, should be made the head of a thousand.

verses.sanskrit: यथा मुख्यान्संनिपात्य वक्तव्याः संशपामहे। विजयार्थं हि संग्रामे न त्यक्ष्यामः परस्परम्॥३२॥
verses.english: Gathering together the leading warriors, they should be addressed, saying,-Let us swear to conquer, and never to leave one another!

verses.sanskrit: इहैव ते निवर्तन्तां ये च केचन भीरवः। ये घातयेयुः प्रवरं कुर्वाणास्तुमुलं प्रति॥३३॥
verses.english: Let those, who are afraid of their life, remain where they are. Let those also stay behind who would cause their chiefs to be killed by themselves neglecting to act heroically in the thick of the fray!

verses.sanskrit: न सन्निपाते प्रदरं वधं वा कुर्युरीदृशाः। आत्मानं च स्वपक्षं च पालयन्हन्ति संयुगे॥३४॥
verses.english: Let such men only come as would never retreat from battle or cause their own comrades to be killed! Protecting their own selves as also their comrades, they are sure to kill the enemy in fight.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थनाशो वधोऽकीर्तिरयशश्च पलायने। अमनोज्ञाऽसुखा वाचः पुरुषस्य पलायने॥३५॥
verses.english: The result of retreating from battle is loss of wealth, death, infamy, and reproach. Unpleasant, sharp and cutting remarks await the fate of him who retreats from battle, who lose his lips and teeth, who casts off all his weapons, or who allows himself to be taken as a captive by the enemy. Let such evil results always befall the warriors of our enemies.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिध्वस्तोष्ठदन्तस्य न्यस्तसर्वायुधस्य च। अमित्रैरवरुद्धस्य द्विषतामस्तु नः सदा॥३६॥
मनुष्यापसदा ह्येते ये भवन्ति पराङ्मुखाः। राशिवर्धनमात्रास्ते नैव ते प्रेत्य नो इह॥३७॥
verses.english: Those who retreat from battle are wretches among men. They simply increase the number of men. They will neither pass in this world nor in the next for true manhood.

verses.sanskrit: अमित्रा हृष्टमनसः प्रत्युद्यान्ति पलायिनम्। जयिनस्तु नरास्तात चन्दनैर्मण्डनेन च॥३८॥
verses.english: Victorious enemies, O Sire, proceed gladly in pursuit of the flying combatants, their praises all the while recited by bards.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य स्म संग्रामगता यशो वै घ्नन्ति शत्रवः। तदसह्यतरं दुःखमहं मन्ये वधादपि॥३९॥
verses.english: When enemies, coming to battle spoil the fame of a person, the misery the latter feels is more piercing, I think, than that of death itself.

verses.sanskrit: जयं जानीत धर्मस्य मूलं सर्वसुखस्य च। या भीरूणां परा ग्लानिः शूरस्तामधिगच्छति॥४०॥
verses.english: Know that victory is the source of religious merit and of every sort of happiness. The heroes bear cheerfully what is regarded as the highest misery by cowards.

verses.sanskrit: ते वयं स्वर्गमिच्छन्तः संग्रामे त्यक्तजीविताः। जयन्तो वध्यमाना वा प्राप्नुयाम च सद्गतिम्॥४१॥
verses.english: Determined upon acquiring heaven we should fight not caring for life itself, and prepared to conquer or die, and we would attain then a blessed end in heaven!

verses.sanskrit: एवं संशप्तशपथाः समभित्यक्तजीविताः। अमित्रवाहिनीं वीराः प्रतिगाहन्त्यभीरवः॥४२॥
verses.english: Having taken such an oath, and prepared to cast away his itself, heroes should bravely rush against the enemy's ranks.

verses.sanskrit: अग्रतः पुरुषानीकमसिचर्मवतां भवेत्। पृष्ठतः शकटानीकं कलत्रं मध्यतस्तथा॥४३॥
verses.english: In the van should be posted a detachment of men armed with swords and shields. In the rear should be planted the car-division. In the interstice should be placed other classes of warriors.

verses.sanskrit: परेषां प्रतिघातार्थं पदातीनां च बृंहणम्। अपि तस्मिन्पुरे वृद्धा भवेयुर्ये पुरोगमाः॥४४॥
verses.english: This should be the arrangement for attacking the enemy. The veterans of the army should fight in the van. They would protect their comrades in the rear.

verses.sanskrit: ये पुरस्तादभिमताः सत्त्ववन्तो मनस्विनः। ते पूर्वमभिवर्तेरंश्चैतानेवेतरे जनाः॥४५॥
verses.english: Those who are the foremost of strength and courage, should be placed in the van. The others should stand behind them.

verses.sanskrit: अपि चोद्धर्षणं कार्यं भीरूणामपि यत्नतः। स्कन्धदर्शनमात्रात्तु तिष्ठेयुर्वा समीपतः॥४६॥
verses.english: The fear-stricken should, with care, be comforted and encouraged. These weaker combatants should be placed on the field only to show the number of the army to the foe.

verses.sanskrit: संहतान्योधयेदल्पान्कामं विस्तारयेद्बहून्। सूचीमुखमनीकं स्यादल्पानां बहुभिः सह॥४७॥
verses.english: If the troops are few, they should be arranged closely for the fight. When necessary, if their leader wishes, the close arrangement may be extended wide. When a small number of soldiers is to fight with a great many, they should be arranged like a needle-point.

verses.sanskrit: सम्प्रयुक्ते निकृष्टे वा सत्यं वा यदि वाऽनृतम्। प्रगृह्य बाहून् क्रोशते भग्ना भग्नाः परे इति॥४८॥
verses.english: When a small army is engaged with a larger one, the leader of the former may shake hands with his men and cry aloud, saying,-The enemy is routed! The enemy is routed!

verses.sanskrit: आगतं मे मित्रबलं प्रहरध्वमभीतवत्। सत्त्ववन्तोऽभिबाधेयुः कुर्वन्तो भैरवान् रवान्॥४९॥
verses.english: The strong amongst them should resist the enemy, loudly saying to their comrades, Fresh friends have arrived! Fearlessly strike at your enemies!

verses.sanskrit: क्ष्वेडाः किलकिलाशब्दाः क्रकचा गोविषाणिकाः। भेरी-मृदङ्ग-पणवा-न्नादयेयुः पुरश्चरान्॥५०॥
verses.english: Those who have gone in advance should utter loud shouts and make various kinds of noises and should blow and beas Krakachas, cow-horns, drums, cymbals, and kettle-drums.'
